text:
maya: Heads-up: planned staggered deployment for runtime + router + console at 22:00 UTC. Canary window 10m, full rollout after green. Need final pin/compat checks from each owner. @sam @jordan @alex @priya

sam: Runtime side: kernel flag default off. New build 3.4.1-rc includes eviction-latch fix. Recommend pinning 3.4.1-rc for canary only and keep 3.4.0 as fallback. Load tests looked ok for 512-token sequences.

jordan: Router: header-split change merged — requires console header contract v2. Alex, can we confirm console handles the split? If not, router can be pinned to previous behaviour via feature flag.

alex: Console: v2 contract is backwards compatible for reads, but the admin UI needs the new header mapping. UI deploy is separate and low-risk; we can delay UI until after canary. Backend is fine.

priya: API: no breaking changes, but we need to ensure the API gateway routing rule TTL is long enough for KV cache warmup during canary. Recommend 1m.

maya: OK — action items: sam pin canary runtime 3.4.1-rc, jordan pin router feature-flagged header-split=false for canary, alex delay UI, priya set gateway TTL=60s. Release notes: mention eviction-latch fix and header-split toggle.

sam: I'll push the runtime canary pin now. Command I used in staging: ```orchctl pin --service runtime --version 3.4.1-rc --scope canary --metadata "eviction_latch=true"```

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by maya in #eng-releases. Next action: initiating canary in 15m.

maya: Canary will be 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 30m if green. Canary SLOs: error rate < 1% sustained, p95 latency increase < 30% vs baseline, no user-facing errors in top-tier customers. Rollback thresholds below.

ops-bot: NOTE: preflight checks passed: infra capacity ok in eu-west-1 and us-east-1.

(15 minutes later)
deploy-bot: Canary start: runtime=3.4.1-rc (10%), router header-split=false (canary), console backend v2, gateway TTL=60s. Monitoring links: https://console/mon/runtimes/3.4.1-rc

jordan: Seeing a small increase in routed queuing on p95 for a subset of routes (service: auth-proxy). p95 up +45ms.

sam: Watching kernel logs — a few KV eviction spikes during warmup. Not steady.

alex: Admin API error spike: 0.6% -> 1.8% for ~90s, mostly 502s from console -> router handshake timing out.

maya: This is within the canary watch window but close to threshold. Reminder: rollback if error rate > 2% for 3 consecutive minutes OR p95 > 300ms for 2 minutes.

jordan: p95 routing for auth-proxy just hit 320ms sustained 2m.

priya: Customer-facing errors rising on a small subset of production keys. Federation vendor alerted (sla).

maya: Decision time — do we continue or rollback? Current signals: p95 breach + vendor alert + increasing 502s. I'm calling rollback. Sam, Jordan, execute rollback plan now.

sam: Rolling runtime back to pinned 3.4.0. Running: ```orchctl rollback --service runtime --to-version 3.4.0 --reason "canary p95 & vendor errors"```

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for runtime. Canary halted. Notifying routing to unpin feature flag.
jordan: Reverting router flag: ```orchctl set-flag router header-split false --scope global --source canary-revert``` — done.

ops-bot: DB connections normalized; eviction spikes subsided. Monitoring shows p95 back under baseline in 90s.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed. runtime -> 3.4.0. Router flag confirmed false. Canary aborted.

maya: Thanks all. Postmortem notes: do a deeper root-cause for console handshake timeouts with header-split interactions and warmup KV patterns on runtime. Update release notes to mark 3.4.1-rc as "blocked: needs further perf tuning".

alex: I'll add a short note to the release doc and add a quick UI toggle to delay admin UI apply.

sam: Follow-ups: add controlled KV warmup in runtime and extend canary ramp by 5m next try. Also add a runtime metric for eviction burst count to alert earlier.

maya: Final: rollback executed and cluster stable. I'll schedule a post-deploy sync for tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Thanks :thumbsup:

priya: Leaving a stub for release notes: [Eviction latch candidate rolled back after canary — see postmortem].

deploy-bot: Thread closed by maya.
